n: The gatekeepers are organized next. They guarded the temple entrances, protected its treasures and kept order. Meshelemiah came from the Korahite family.

f.g: Gatekeepers, not baggage carriers.
Probably Ebiasaph, a Korahite ancestor (1 Chronicles 9:19), not Asaph the musician.

n: Meshelemiah’s sons are listed in birth order, beginning with Zechariah, who guarded the tent of meeting.
Meshelemiah’s fifth through seventh sons complete his family.

f.g: The full form of the name John, “the LORD is gracious.”

n: Obed-edom—whose house sheltered the ark for three months—had many sons who became gatekeepers.
Obed-edom had eight sons “for God blessed him.” The blessing promised when the ark stayed in his house is seen in his large family.
Obed-edom’s grandsons through Shemaiah became leaders of their family because of their ability.

f.g: Capable, strong men—here suited to guard duty.

n: Shemaiah’s sons and relatives, all strong and capable.

f.g: “He is my God”; also the name of Job’s young friend (Job 32:2).

n: Obed-edom’s family supplied sixty-two capable gatekeepers—the largest group.

f.g: Sixty-two.
Strong, qualified men for the work.

n: Meshelemiah’s family supplied eighteen.

f.g: Together with the other families, about ninety-three senior gatekeepers are named.

n: Hosah, a Merarite, made his son Simri chief even though he was not the firstborn—perhaps because of his ability or because the firstborn had died.

f.w: though he was not the firstborn

n: Hosah’s other sons are listed; his family numbered thirteen.

f.g: A Levite gatekeeper, not the later high priest.

n: These leaders formed the gatekeeper divisions, serving in shifts just like their fellow Levites.

f.g: Taking turns in duty shifts, matched to their brethren.

n: They cast lots for each gate, small families and large alike, ensuring fairness.

f.w: as well the small as the great

n: The east gate—the main entrance—went to Shelemiah (Meshelemiah). The north went to his son Zechariah, praised as a wise counselor.

f.g: Same as Meshelemiah (verse 1).
A man of good judgment; gatekeepers needed wisdom as well as strength.

n: The south gate went to Obed-edom, and his sons guarded the storehouse.

f.g: “Storehouses”—buildings for temple supplies.

n: The west gate, called Shallecheth, on the road going up, went to Shuppim and Hosah.

f.g: A gate name meaning possibly “casting out,” perhaps where refuse was taken out.

f.w: the causeway of the going up
f.g: An ascending road or ramp leading to the temple.

n: The daily guard: six at the east, four at the north and south, and two pairs at the storehouse.

f.g: The east gate, facing the main approach, received the largest guard.

n: On the west side, four guarded the road and two guarded the Parbar, making twenty-four posts in all.

f.g: A colonnade or court on the temple’s west side; the exact meaning is uncertain.

n: These were the gatekeeper divisions from the families of Korah and Merari.

f.g: Korahites, descendants of Korah through Kore.

n: Other Levites were placed over the temple treasuries and the dedicated gifts.

f.w: the treasures of the dedicated things
f.g: Gifts consecrated to God, such as war plunder set apart for the temple.

n: Gershonite Levites of Laadan’s family, led by Jehieli, oversaw treasuries.

f.g: Probably the same as Jehiel (1 Chronicles 23:8).

n: Jehieli’s sons Zetham and Joel were in charge of the temple treasury.
Next come the Kohathite families: the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites and Uzzielites.

f.g: Descendants of Amram, father of Moses and Aaron.

n: Shebuel, a descendant of Moses, was chief officer over the treasuries.

f.w: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses
f.g: “Son” here means descendant; many generations lie between.

n: Through Moses’ other son Eliezer came a line leading to Shelomith.
Shelomith and his relatives managed all the treasures dedicated by David and his military leaders.

f.g: Army officers commanding large and small units.

n: These treasures came from plunder won in battle and were dedicated to maintain the Lord’s house. Victories God gave were returned to God.

f.w: Out of the spoils won in battles

n: Gifts dedicated by Samuel, Saul, Abner and Joab were also under Shelomith’s care. Generations of leaders had contributed to God’s house.
Chenaniah and his sons from the Izharites handled duties outside the temple, serving as officials and judges across Israel.

f.g: Work outside the temple—civil administration and judging.

n: Hashabiah and 1,700 Hebronites served west of the Jordan in both religious and royal affairs. Spiritual and civic service went hand in hand.

f.w: in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king

n: In David’s fortieth and final year, a search of records found capable Hebronite men at Jazer in Gilead, east of the Jordan.

f.w: the fortieth year of the reign of David
f.g: David’s last year, about 970 BC.

n: David appointed 2,700 of them as leaders over the tribes east of the Jordan for all matters of God and of the king—ensuring the distant tribes were not neglected.

f.w: every matter pertaining to God, and affairs of the king
